reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm target engagement for any of the compounds (pemetrexed, carboplatin, paclitaxel, bevacizumab). Standard doses were used (pemetrexed 500 mg/m², carboplatin AUC 6, paclitaxel 200 mg/m², bevacizumab 15 mg/kg) which are within established therapeutic ranges, suggesting adequate exposure was likely achieved. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or pharmacodynamic markers reported to assess whether targets drove their intended mechanisms (antifolate inhibition, DNA crosslinking, microtubule stabilization, angiogenesis inhibition). 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Both arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of progression-free survival without grade 4 toxicity. Pemetrexed+carboplatin arm achieved 3.91 months median G4PFS vs 2.86 months for paclitaxel+carboplatin+bevacizumab arm (p=0.176, not significant). Neither regimen demonstrated clinical benefit. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial appears adequately powered (N=361) and conducted for sufficient duration (171.6 weeks). Safety profiles were manageable with expected toxicities for each regimen. This appears to be a straightforward efficacy failure where neither combination regimen provided meaningful clinical benefit in advanced NSCLC.

failure_modes.evidence: Both combination regimens used established compounds at standard doses likely to engage their targets and modulate intended pathways, but neither achieved clinical benefit on the primary endpoint (G4PFS 3.91 vs 2.86 months, p=0.176)
